messages:
deploy-bot: deploy finished: canary rollout started for model=redwood-open-7b-hotpatch, tag=hotpatch-2024-04-04, cluster=us-west-2-canary :package:

Alice Nguyen: heads up — canary logs showing tokenizer errors, a bunch of "�" characters and truncated tokens in responses. seeing odd token counts in traces.

Alice Nguyen: sample: `User: summarize
Model: 
�Did not parse` — looks like tokenizer and weight mismatch.

Rob Kim: paging Priya (oncall) — this is generating 5xx-style failures at the inference gateway for ~2% of requests to canary.

incident-bot: SEV-2 incident created: INC-2024-1853. PagerDuty alerted Priya Patel.

Priya Patel: on it. what's customer impact? any enterprise customers hit?

Alice Nguyen: initial metric: error-rate on canary up from 0.2% to 12% for streaming endpoints. throughput fine. small set of request shapes fail (longer prefixes). I flagged a customer error id that hit an enterprise account — CS alerted.

Priya Patel: ok — immediate mitigation: roll back canary or flip feature flag to stop canary traffic. Which is faster?

Leah Ortiz: flipping traffic split flag is fastest. I can flip the canary flag to 100% -> stable, effectively stopping hotpatch traffic. Command:

```
# flip feature flag to stop canary
curl -X POST https://console.redwood.ai/api/flags/rollout -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"feature":"model_canary","value":"stable"}'
```

Leah Ortiz: I'll run it if folks ack.

Marco Silva: +1 flip. Also we should prepare a rollback of the weightset if the flag flip doesn't fully stop all traffic. suspect weight/tokenizer bundle mismatch: tokenization assets missing in hotpatch bundle.

Priya Patel: Leah, flip now. Post logs.

Leah Ortiz: done. feature flag flipped at 12:07 UTC. response: 200 OK.

Alice Nguyen: within ~30s errors dropped to baseline. streaming responses for new canary requests now look normal (no garbled tokens). But we still have ~40 traces from earlier that bubbled into logs.

incident-bot: automation note — traffic re-routed off hotpatch canary. Canary instances will be drained per policy.

Rob Kim: can we confirm root cause before re-rolling? any config diffs between hotpatch bundle and stable bundle?

Alice Nguyen: pulling diffs now. quick grep shows tokenizer_version in model config: hotpatch bundle: `tokenizer: { version: "v1" }` stable: `tokenizer: { version: "v2", merges: "bpe_v2.merges" }`. hotpatch missing merges file in /model/assets.

Marco Silva: that explains it — weights were hotpatched but tokenizer assets not included in the bundle. Some encodings changed between v1 and v2 so mismatch causes broken decoding for longer sequences.

Priya Patel: action items: 1) ensure canary stopped (done), 2) rollback hotpatch from canary -> also remove from rollout plan, 3) assess customer impact and notify CS.

Leah Ortiz: I'll remove hotpatch tag from the rollout manifest and mark hotpatch-2024-04-04 as bad. Command I ran:

```
redwoodctl rollout abort --tag hotpatch-2024-04-04 --scope canary
```

Leah Ortiz: abort returned OK and rollout plan updated.

Alice Nguyen: starting a scripted scan to find any model bundles with missing tokenizer assets across regions.

Marco Silva: we should also create a short-lived validation that checks model bundle contains tokenizer merges/vocab if model config references them. I'll open an infra PR after this.

Priya Patel: CS: @customer-success-bot can you open a customer note for the impacted enterprise account and set to P0 outreach? include timeline and mitigation.

customer-success-bot: created CS-TICKET-8345 assigned to Jenna. Notifying account owner.

Rob Kim: any errors on the runtime side? no memory spikes or kernel faults?

Alice Nguyen: runtime metrics look stable. only decoder errors and malformed tokens. weight loads succeeded; it's purely asset mismatch.

Marco Silva: root cause hypothesis: CI artifact step omitted tokenizer assets when packaging hotpatch bundle due to a missing glob. CI job: `package-model --include weights/* --include tokenizer/*` — turned out tokenizer/* expanded empty for this tag (tokenizer/v2 path mismatch). Patch in CI needed.

Priya Patel: escalate to eng-runtime: assign to Marco + Leah for fix and rollout guidance. I'll update incident ticket and keep as SEV-2 until follow-ups done.

Leah Ortiz: re-run integration test locally: verified that new package script includes merges and vocab. I have a patched CI commit ready: `ci: require tokenizer assets or fail` — will open PR 4876 now.

Alice Nguyen: for immediate safety, add pre-deploy check in deploy bot: if model config references tokenizer assets, verify artifact contains them before push.

incident-bot: added runbook task: "Add tokenizer artifact validation to model packaging and deploy checks" to INC-2024-1853 checklist.

Marco Silva: plan for re-release: 1) patch CI, 2) rebuild hotpatch bundle with tokenizer assets, 3) test in isolated canary (no traffic), 4) run compatibility test harness across short/long prefixes, 5) small canary roll, monitor for 60m.

Priya Patel: agree. timeline estimate: patch and rebuild in next 90m, isolated tests 30m, canary re-roll 1h monitoring. I'll coordinate with release schedule.

Leah Ortiz: PR 4876 opened. CI gate added to require tokenizer files when config references them.

Rob Kim: customer impact summary for postmortem: ~2% of canary traffic affected, ~12% error-rate on canary while hotpatch active, one enterprise account had 42 failed requests over 20 minutes. No data exfiltration, no persisted corruption.

Priya Patel: handing off remaining work to eng-runtime. I'll remove pager once the re-release completes and validation checks are merged.

Marco Silva: taking ownership for rollout vetting and postmortem. Assigning follow-ups: M-1 validate CI change merged and green; M-2 rebuild hotpatch bundle; M-3 run compatibility suite; M-4 update deploy runbook.

Leah Ortiz: noted. I'll coordinate the rebuild and isolated tests.

Priya Patel: closing immediate page. marking incident as mitigated (canary traffic stopped). leaving SEV-2 open for follow-up tasks.

incident-bot: incident INC-2024-1853 status updated to MITIGATED (reduction of canary error-rate, traffic routed back to stable).

Alice Nguyen: quick comms draft for slack #general and for affected customers: posting after CS review.

customer-success-bot: CS outreach in progress.

Priya Patel: on-call handoff: I'm signing out at 13:00 UTC. Rob, you'll be SRE handover if anything pops.

Rob Kim: ack. I'll monitor re-roll progress and the CI PR.

Marco Silva: leaving a link to the follow-up ticket: DOCS-2198 for runbook + RM-321 for rollback automation.

Leah Ortiz: final note: steps to prevent recurrence added to checklist and PR description. will add test vectors that exercise tokenizer v1->v2 edge cases.

Alice Nguyen: thanks everyone. postmortem owner: Marco. expected write-up due EOD tomorrow.

Priya Patel: thanks team. incident thread closed for now.
